title: IG&H fell from v2 top pick to conversion target because OutSystems Premier fills the slot
content:
IG&H was a top pick in the v2 ranking and is now filed do-not-pitch. The vertical fit did not change and is still described as excellent; what changed is that OutSystems Premier status was recognised as slot occupancy. The app layer a Powerhouse engagement would occupy is already held by a proprietary competitor, and Premier is the deepest tier of that relationship rather than a casual one.

This is the clearest example in the cohort of one criterion overriding all the others. Vertical fit, size and geography are the attributes that make a lead pleasant to work with; slot occupancy decides whether there is anything to sell. A Premier partner has certification investment, co-selling motions and pipeline attached to the incumbent platform, so a competing layer arrives as a threat to the practice rather than an addition to it.

The residual value recorded is conversion at best — the same demotion path as ITSector in Portugal. That reframes the engagement from partnership to displacement, which needs a different pitch, a different sponsor inside the firm, and a much longer horizon than the current pipeline supports.
